questions.q: Number of hydrogen atoms per molecule of a hydrocarbon A having $85 . 8 %$~carbon is (Given : Molar mass of $A = 84g{mol}^{- 1}$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Using table of empirical formula for the compound:
Element Percentage Mole ratio
C $85 . 8$ $\dfrac{85 . 8}{12} = 7 . 15$ $1$
H $14 . 2$ $\dfrac{14 . 2}{1} = 14 . 2$ $2$

~

Thus, empirical formula is~ \left({CH}_{2}\right)$, empirical molecular mass = 14
Thus,~$\dfrac{MolecularMass}{EmpiricalMass} = n$

questions.q:
$100mL$ of ${Na}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ solution contains $3 . 45g$ of sodium. The molarity of the solution is .....$\times {10}^{- 2}molL^{- 1}$. (Nearest integer)
[Atomic Masses - $Na: 23 . 0u, O: 16 . 0u, P: 31 . 0u ]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Number of mole of ${Na}^{+}$ ion $= \dfrac{3 . 45}{23}mol$

So number of mole of ${Na}_{3}{PO}_{4} = \dfrac{3 . 45}{3 \times 23} = 0 . 050mol$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $93 \mathrm{~g}$ of aniline produces $330 \mathrm{~g}$ of $2,4,6-$ tribromoaniline. Hence $9.3 \mathrm{~g}$ of aniline should produce $33 \mathrm{~g}$ of 2, 4, 6-tribromoaniline. Hence percentage yield $\frac{26.4 \times 100}{33}=80 \%$

questions.q: $CNG$ is an important transportation fuel. When $100gCNG$ is mixed with $208g$ oxygen in vehicles, it leads to the formation of ${CO}_{2}$ and ${H}_{2}O$ and produces large quantity of heat during this combustion, then the amount of carbon dioxide, produced in grams is [nearest integer] [Assume CNG to be methane]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${CH}_{4} + 2{O}_{2} ⟶ {CO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

$\dfrac{100}{16}\dfrac{208}{32}$

$\dfrac{Numberofmoles}{stoichiometriccoefficient}for{CH}_{4} = \dfrac{6 . 25}{1}\dfrac{Numberofmoles}{stoichiometriccoefficient}for{O}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2} = 3 . 25$

The reagent with lower ratio of number of moles to stoichiometric coefficient is called limiting reagent.

Hence, ${O}_{2}$ is limiting reagent

Limiting reagent decides the amount of product,

As per the equation~2 moles of~${O}_{2}$~gives rise to 1 mole of~${CO}_{2}$, So 6.5 moles of~${O}_{2}$~gives~$\dfrac{6 . 5}{2}$~moles of~${CO}_{2}$

$⇒ {nCO}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2}$

So mass of~${CO}_{2} = \dfrac{6 . 5}{2} \times 44 = 143gm$

$[$Molar mass of $KCl = 74 . 5g ]$

questions.solution:
Molality \left(m\right) = \left\{\dfrac{M \times 1000}{1000 \times d - M \times {M}_{solute }}\right\}$

$3 . 3 = \dfrac{M \times 1000}{1000 \times 1 . 20 - M \times 74 . 5}$

$3960 - 245 . 85M = 1000M$

$1245 . 85M = 3960$

$M = \dfrac{3960}{1245 . 85} = 3 . 17 \approx 3M$

$

questions.q:
$116g$ of a substance upon dissociation reaction, yields $7 . 5g$ of hydrogen, $60g$ of oxygen and $48 . 5g$ of carbon. Given that the atomic masses of $H, O$ and $C$ are $1, 16$ and $12$, respectively. The data agrees with how many formulae of the following?

A.~${CH}_{3}COOH$

B.~$HCHO$

C.~${CH}_{3}{OOCH}_{3}$

D.~${CH}_{3}CHO$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
\left(OrganicCompoundcontaingC, H, O\right)\overset{dissociati on}{⟶}\mathop{H}_{7 . 5gram} + \mathop{O}_{60gram} + \mathop{C}_{48 . 5gram}%$ of $H$ in~the given organic compound~$= \dfrac{7 . 5}{116} \times 100 = 6 . 465 %$

(A)~$%$~of~$H = \dfrac{4}{60} \times 100 = 6 . 6 %$

(B)~$%$~of~$H = \dfrac{2}{30} \times 100 = 6 . 6$%

(c)~$%$~of~$H = \dfrac{6}{62} \times 100 = 7 . 677$%

(D)~$%$~of~$H = \dfrac{4}{44} \times 100 = 9 . 09$%

The percentage of Hydrogen in the given organic compound is equal to~$6 . 465 %$~which is approximately equal to the percentage of hydrogen in~${CH}_{3}COOHandHCHO$.

$

questions.q: $10mL$ of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion gives $40mL$ of ${CO}_{2}  \left(g\right)$ and $50mL of water vapour. Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is _______.$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction can be represented as

${C}_{x}{H}_{y} + \left(x + \dfrac{y}{4}\right){O}_{2} \to {xCO}_{2} + {yH}_{2}O$

At STP, $1$ mole of any gas occupies $22 . 4L$

$10mL$ of hydrocarbon, $50mL$ of water and $40mL$ of carbon dioxide corresponds to $0 . 45, 2 . 23$, and $1 . 79$moles respectively.

Hence, the combustion of $1$ mole of hydrocarbon will produce $5$ moles of water and $4$ moles of carbon dioxide.

Thus, the molecular formula contains $4$ carbon atoms and $10$ hydrogen atoms.

The hydrocarbon is ${C}_{4}{H}_{10}$ and the combustion reaction is

${C}_{4}{H}_{10} + 6 . 5{O}_{2} \to 4{CO}_{2} + 5{H}_{2}O$

$x + y = 4 + 10 = 14$

Hence the Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is $14$.

questions.q: When $800mL$ of $0 . 5M$ nitric acid is heated in a beaker, its volume is reduced to half and $11 . 5g$ of nitric acid is evaporated. The molarity of the remaining nitric acid solution is $x \times {10}^{- 2}M$. (Molar mass of nitric acid is $63g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The number of moles of nitric acid,& ${n}_{HNO3} = 0 . 5 \times 0 . 8$

$= 0 . 4mole$

\left({n}_{HNO3}\right)remains = 0 . 4 - \dfrac{11 . 5}{63}$

$= 0 . 4 - 0 . 1825$

$= 0 . 2175$

Molarity~$= \dfrac{0 . 2175}{400} \times 1000$

$= \dfrac{0 . 2175}{0 . 4}$

$= 0 . 5437mole / lit .$

$≃ 0 . 54mole / lit .$

$= 54 \times {10}^{- 2}mol / lit .$

$

questions.q: In the above reaction, $5g$ of toluene is converted into benzaldehyde with $92 %$ yield. The amount of benzaldehyde produced is____~$× {10}^{- 2}g$
